$description: Navigator › Data: the value tree under one state entry — what the canvas resolved that entry to, a line per key. The rows arrive FLAT. JSON nests to any depth and a document's one repeater is `$prototype: "Array"` over a list, so `panels/data-explorer.ts` walks the value once, applies the item, key and depth caps, and hands over rows that already carry their own indent; recursion is a property of the walk rather than of the markup. Two kinds of line come out of it: a key and the value beside it, and a truncation marker, which is a real button because the reader opened this panel BECAUSE item 40 was the surprising one. The adapter decides what a value reads as and what a marker raises; nothing here knows about the canvas.

style.$description: The whole of the tree's look, and two things about it are the conversion. THE SYNTAX COLOURS MOVED: `--data-key` was declared on `<sp-theme>` in `styles/spectrum.css`, where Spectrum's own ramp is in scope, and this document is mounted in the Navigator — outside that element every `var(--data-key)` would have silently taken its hex fallback and stopped following the theme, so the key colour is `var(--accent)`, which is the studio token `--spectrum-blue-700` was chosen to match. Its three neighbours (`--data-string`, `--data-number`, `--data-boolean`) are NOT re-pointed, because no rule ever read them: they were declared for a palette nobody wrote, and inventing one here would be a visual change nobody asked for. `data-tone` still carries the type on every value, so the day that palette is designed it has somewhere to land. AND THE INDENT IS A VARIABLE: a row's depth used to be an inline `style="padding-left:…"`, which is one rule per row once the padding is a declaration; `--row-indent` is written inline under its own name and read by one shared rule, so a hundred-row tree interns one.

& [part=\"row\"], & [part=\"more\"].$description: Every line, whichever kind. One line high and clipped rather than wrapped: a tree that reflows a long string across three lines stops being a column of keys you can scan.

& [part=\"key\"].$description: The key or index this line is under. Empty for the single line a primitive value renders as, which is why it is always drawn: a span with nothing in it takes no width, and switching it in and out would cost a wrapper element per row to save nothing.

& [part=\"value\"][data-tone=\"null\"],.$description: Not a value you are reading: an absence, or a summary standing in for the lines underneath it. Both are dimmed and italic so the eye passes over them on the way to what is real.

& [part=\"more\"].$description: A truncation marker is a CONTROL, not a caption — it shows more of what the panel already has in hand. Dressed as the text it replaced so the tree does not sprout buttons, and stripped of the chrome a `<button>` brings with it, but focusable and hoverable so that it reads as pressable.
